idiom_name: fragment functions returning markup (template literals), engine partials where templates are files
implementation_notes: The simpler local idiom replaces the include machinery: a fragment is a function returning markup (a template literal, or a JSX element under a renderer), composed by calling and nesting it from the page function - no registration, no ambient context, and the function signature is the fragment's interface. When markup stays in files (Express view engines), the pattern is provided for you: EJS includes with <%- include('user/show', {user}) %> resolved relative to the including template, Pug's include resolved at compile time, and Handlebars partials registered once with Handlebars.registerPartial and called as {{> myPartial}} (dynamic names via a subexpression plus the lookup helper). Choose functions when layout is code, engine partials when designers own the templates.
pitfalls: Template literals interpolate raw: an unescaped ${value} is an XSS hole - escape every interpolated fragment input, or use the engine's escaped output tag (<%= %>) instead of the raw one (<%- %>).
EJS include paths are strings resolved relative to the including template and require the filename option for caching; typos surface as runtime errors on the request that renders the page.

Handlebars partials live in one global registry: two views registering the same partial name silently override each other, and an unknown {{> name}} throws at render time unless a partial block provides a fallback.
